name: DMRT3 (gait)
summary: DMRT3, the "gait keeper", on chromosome 23: the main known gene behind the extra gaits of gaited horses. One base change (g.22,999,655C>A, Ser301STOP) cuts the protein short and alters the spinal circuits that time the limbs. The derived allele A makes lateral gaits - amble, tolt, rack, pace - easier, and hinders the change from trot or pace to gallop; C is the ancestral allele. It is permissive, not decisive: an A/A horse can still trot, and which gait a horse actually performs depends on other genes, conformation and training. In Icelandic Horses, A/A horses tend to have five gaits including pace, while C/A horses score better in walk, trot, canter and gallop. It is not a general speed gene, though A/A Standardbreds do better in harness racing. Found in 68 of 141 breeds tested, and common mainly in gaited and harness-racing breeds.

phenotypes.name: Gaited
phenotypes.description: Two A copies. The strongest predisposition to lateral gaits - tolt, rack, pace - and, in Icelandic Horses, to five gaits including pace. The change from trot or pace to gallop may be harder, and the conventional gaits tend to score lower than with one copy. Which gait appears is not set by this locus.

phenotypes.name: One gait copy
phenotypes.description: One A copy. Some tendency to amble while keeping strong conventional gaits: in Icelandic Horses these score better in walk, trot, canter and gallop than horses with two copies, and are more likely to have four gaits, without pace.

phenotypes.name: No gait copy
phenotypes.description: No A copy. The usual walk, trot and canter; lateral gaits and pace are less likely, though not impossible.

frequencies.population: Icelandic Horse (allele frequency of A about 0.94 in the 2012 population studied; genotype shares worked out from it)
